matt: Heads up — ran a nightly kernel inventory vs runtime probe and found a discrepancy on amd-renderers-02. Some kernels listed in the model kernel matrix aren't present on the node image.
anya: ugh. which kernels?
matt: specifically: `attn_fused_v2_sm80` shows in the matrix for seq_len 128/256 but on that fleet node only `attn_generic_fp16` and `attn_tiled_sm75` are installed.
kevin: that would trigger conditional routing to generic path, right? 
anya: yeah fallback to `attn_generic_fp16` for AMD when autoselect doesn't find the architecture-aware kernel. That explains the latency spike we saw on nightly perf tests for seq=128.
matt: here's the probe output (from /opt/runtime/bin/kernel-check):
```
KERNEL_MATRIX: model_xx_v2 -> attn_fused_v2_sm80 (expected: sm80,sm75)
NODE_KERNELS: [attn_generic_fp16, attn_tiled_sm75]
RESULT: missing: attn_fused_v2_sm80
```
oliver: timeline: when did the node image get built? maybe packaging step dropped the roc-optimized kernels.
ci-bot: build/ami-2026-03-15 completed for amd-renderers-02 (artifacts: base-runtime, kernels-v1.4.2) :white_check_mark:
matt: AMI shows kernels-v1.4.2 but we recently hotpatched kernels-v1.5.0 to staging images. looks like that roll didn't finish for this group.
kevin: Perf numbers I pulled from the canary traces: p50/generation for seq=128 on model_xx_v2 was ~42ms on host with fused kernel, ~98ms on hosts without it. p95 shows ~180ms vs ~420ms. KV cache hit-rate also dropped ~6% because the fallback path evicts earlier (different cache shaping).
anya: who owns the kernel packaging? @oliver?
oliver: I own packaging. I did a trimmed build to reduce image size and accidentally excluded the sm80 fused bundle. My bad.
matt: we should do two things: 1) add a defensive conditional-route rule so that if a kernel listed in the matrix is missing we prefer a nearer-compatible kernel variant (e.g., `attn_tiled_sm75`) instead of generic, and 2) add an alert when kernel inventory diverges from matrix.
kevin: agreed. Also add a quick autotune entry that pins sequence-length thresholds so scheduler chooses the tiled route for seq <= 256 on AMD before falling back. That should avoid the KV cache thrash.
anya: low-risk plan: oliver patches AMI to include kernels-v1.5.0, trigger rolling update for amd-renderers-02; runtime team will push a conditional-route rule in staging to prefer tiled_sm75 when fused is missing.
ci-bot: creating issue RK-4723: "AMI: include kernels-v1.5.0 on amd-renderers-02" assigned to oliver.
oliver: ETA for AMI patch = today EOD. I'll coordinate with infra for a staged rollout.
matt: runtime-side PR idea (pseudo):
```
if kernel_available(model, arch, wanted='attn_fused_v2_sm80'):
  route('fused_sm80')
elif kernel_available(model, arch, alt='attn_tiled_sm75'):
  route('tiled_sm75')
else:
  route('generic_fp16')
```
kevin: also add an autotune entry: `autotune[model_xx_v2][amd] = [{max_seq:256, prefer: tiled_sm75}]`
anya: I'll add the alert: `kernel-matrix-divergence` when missing count > 0 for >10m per nodegroup.
matt: one more note — logs show this discrepancy only on one nodegroup; fine to roll that subset first. We should also run a quick bench after AMI patch: run `perfbench --model model_xx_v2 --seq 128 --runs 200 --nodes amd-renderers-02` and check p50/p95 + kv-hit-rate.
oliver: starting AMI build now. I'll post when images are up.
kevin: thanks — will open runtime PR and autotune entry after lunch.
anya: thanks team :thumbsup:
matt: follow-ups: oliver (AMI), kevin (runtime PR + autotune), anya (alert). We'll reconvene in this thread when the bench runs finish.
